dimensions.assessment: Affects federal contractors, executive agencies, the Department of Defense, and workers on federal projects nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: The head of an executive agency may not require or give preference to an offeror on the basis of whether the offeror will use workers subject to a collective bargaining agreement.

dimensions.assessment: Changes contracting rules by barring union preferences or requirements, altering bidding conditions for affected contractors.
dimensions.evidence: prohibit a requirement or preference for the use of union labor for Federal contracts.

dimensions.assessment: May affect federal contract bidding costs and competition, though specific dollar impacts are not stated.
Amends titles 41 and 10 of the United States Code regarding federal and defense procurement rules.
dimensions.evidence: To amend titles 41 and 10, United States Code, to prohibit a requirement or preference for the use of union labor for Federal contracts.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory prohibition on union requirements or preferences in federal procurement.

importance_detail.rationale: Prohibits executive agencies and the Department of Defense from requiring or giving preference to union labor or collective bargaining agreements in federal contracts.
